0.content:
Cacucu is a small, round, pink juvenile Qucusaur with a white eyepatch over his left eye. He can grow wings like an adult Qucusaur. He is Ifa's assistant at the clinic and calls himself Ifa's "brother". He understands human speech and body language well, but his vocal cords limit him to repeating phrases he picked up from Ifa ("No way, bro!", "For real, now? Do you even hear yourself, bro?", "Hit me up, bro!"). When the Traveler indwells a saurian he speaks fluently, insists he is a colleague, not a pet, and asks to be called Dr. Cacucu. Ifa found him being bullied by other saurians for his odd looks, pecked and bleeding, and treated him; Cacucu has stuck to him ever since. He once caught a fever from a sick patient and nearly died despite everything Ifa did.

Ifa's Character Story 4 reveals what Ifa does not know. Cacucu first saw Ifa on hatching: Ifa had treated his badly injured mother, who might never have hatched him otherwise. After she died of old injuries, Cacucu chose Ifa. With Ororon as accomplice he pecked holes in Ororon's vegetables so Ororon could accuse Ifa, cornering Ifa into taking him in as compensation, plus a month as Ororon's courier. He keeps his history to himself so that Ifa, who shoulders others' burdens, will not take him in out of guilt.

1.content:
Ororon of the Masters of the Night-Wind is Ifa's closest friend. Ifa thinks he has "a very peculiar way of thinking": you go with the flow and stop trying to figure him out, though some days Ifa wishes he could see inside his head. Ororon relaxes around Ifa, jokes and says "bro". Ifa delivers his vegetables, fruit and Phlogiston Aphid honey to Citlali and the Children of Echoes, and Ororon painted the placard outside Ifa's clinic. Ifa insists he did not paint it himself.

In Ororon's memories (5.1), Ifa catches him overwatering radishes. Asked whether being a vet is fun, Ifa says most people have no special purpose or calling. Then he admits the fun part is outsmarting rascally patients and drags Ororon in to help. The remark echoed back to Ororon in his darkest moment. Ifa calls Ororon stubborner than any patient, yet trusts him to manage whatever the world throws at him.

2.comment: Ifa: Citlali and the gem delivery
2.content:
Ifa often brings Ororon's vegetables to Citlali, whom he calls "Granny": a "tough cookie" with a colourful pajama collection. He passes messages on word for word with no questions, to stay out of the line of fire. During the Archon Quest (5.1), when Ororon was avoiding her while working with the Fatui Captain, Citlali put the replacement gem for Ororon's soul-stabilising talisman in a supply bag and had Ifa deliver it. Ifa agreed without asking anything. The bag also let Citlali and the Traveler view Ororon's memories. Citlali later told Ororon to thank Ifa sometime.

Ifa never learned the second purpose of the bag. Earlier, Citlali had snapped that Ororon could stop "sending Ifa over" with his vegetables, which is how Paimon first heard his name. At the Masters of the Night-Wind, an angry Citlali once pointed at Ifa while chasing Ororon, who was practising "invisibility arts" behind passers-by. Ifa's honest bewilderment ("what are 'invisibility arts'?") calmed her.

3.comment: Ifa: Nampole, Antu and the Medicine Born of Guilt
3.content:
During the limited-time Tournament of Glory in Bloom (5.5), Ifa diagnosed the young Tepetlisaur Milray, a war hero, with a rare phlogiston illness caused by overusing phlogiston too young. The cure needed Ocean Zephyrs and Sacred Flame Crystals, so Mavuika revived the Bloomflower Trials. A silent ghost Qucusaur, Antu, followed Ifa and led the group to buried scrolls by Nampole. These showed that centuries ago Nampole, a Flower-Feather sauro-vet and Ifa's ancestor, sought the same cure for Antu. His brother, Chief Imara, turned the Trials into a bloodbath and kept the crystals; Antu died believing the crystals corrupt hearts and blaming himself. Nampole spent his life healing saurians: the "medicine born of guilt" Ifa's father had mentioned.

Ifa realised that young saurians, like children, want to help and hate feeling like a burden. So instead of telling Antu the truth, he staged a show: the tribes faked a crystal-induced quarrel, Ororon added black mist, and Antu cast a "Spell of Unity" that Ifa had taught him. Milray took the medicine, and Antu, at peace, departed for the Night Kingdom. Ifa told Nampole's spirit he understood the guilt, because Cacucu had once nearly died in his care, and promised to keep improving the family medicine so no one would feel it again.

4.comment: Ifa: Chasca, the Flower-Feather Clan and Ineffa
4.content: Ifa is a vet of the Flower-Feather Clan, the flying tribe of Qucusaur riders. Chasca's father and Chuychu have discussed medicine with him many times. When Chasca brought her saurian Coya for a checkup, he glanced at it, said it was nothing serious and Cusco could handle it, and rushed off to another patient. She admits he was right. In Flamelets (5.8), Chasca brought him a Qucusaur wounded by Secret Source automatons. He then joined the patrol "just in case" and examined the unconscious woman they found on the beach; unsure he was "qualified for this", he showed the others that she was a machine. Beside her he found a cryptex marked with drawings of the Traveler and Paimon, and warned that it would self-destruct if forced. He returned to the clinic to watch his patient.

5.content: Kinich once brought Ajaw to Ifa, claiming the self-styled "Almighty Dragonlord" was ill and ranting. Ifa examined him thoroughly, found nothing wrong and advised Kinich to "bash him on the head a few times until he starts working again". Ajaw promptly felt better. Kinich calls Ifa a pro; Ifa wonders whether Ajaw technically counts as a living being. Ajaw and Cacucu feud endlessly, and Cacucu calls Ajaw half a bro. In 5.8, after Kinich put Ajaw in a three-day timeout, Ifa sent Cacucu to pester him for another night until the furious Ajaw let slip "Sovereign ruler"; Citlali says Kinich and Ifa have been keeping watch on him since (Smoldering).

6.comment: Ifa: Xilonen and the saurian syringes
6.content: On his tour of the tribes, Ifa found Xilonen unusually available. She was buried in a commission from Mavuika and welcomed unrelated work, so she designed his medical equipment on the spot. Her saurian syringes are intimidating enough that even rowdy saurians sit still, needle or no needle; Ifa credits them for his calm patients. He loves chatting with her and says intimidation is "a function in its own right". He has also treated Tepetlisaurs at the Children of Echoes.

7.content: The Pyro Archon once gave Ifa a ride to an emergency call. He arrived dizzy and still managed to treat the injured saurian, which taught him we sometimes don't know our potential until pushed. Mavuika says great doctors need observation and empathy as well as knowledge when the patient doesn't share their language, which is why Ifa can befriend almost anyone. Anyone on bad terms with him, she jokes, is probably the problem.
